es.summary: Daño a las células sensoriales del oído interno causado por ciertos fármacos o químicos, que produce pérdida auditiva y alteraciones del equilibrio.
key_points: Aminoglucósidos y vancomicina son los fármacos más frecuentes.
El daño a los cilios cocleares suele ser irreversible.
Los síntomas incluyen tinnitus, pérdida auditiva y vértigo.
Monitorear niveles séricos y función renal reduce el riesgo.
Prevención incluye evitar ruidos fuertes y ajustar dosis.

pathophysiology: Acumulación del fármaco en el líquido endolinfático daña los cilios del cóclea y vestibular.
Se genera estrés oxidativo y apoptosis de células sensoriales.
El daño estructural es frecuentemente irreversible.
La toxicidad vestibular produce vértigo y desequilibrio.
risk_factors: Exposición a solventes (tolueno) o metales pesados.
signs_symptoms: Pérdida auditiva progresiva, inicialmente de altas frecuencias.
Vértigo o sensación de que todo gira.
Náuseas, vómitos y desequilibrio al caminar.
Sensación de plenitud en el oído.
diagnostics: Niveles séricos de vancomicina o aminoglucósidos.
Examen otoscópico para descartar otras causas.
Panel renal (creatinina, BUN) para ajustar dosis.
treatment: Suspender o reducir la dosis del agente ototóxico.
Hidratación adecuada y corrección de función renal.
Terapia auditiva (audífonos) si la pérdida es permanente.
Evitar exposición a ruidos fuertes y ototóxicos adicionales.
complications: Daño vestibular crónico con riesgo de caídas.
Incremento del riesgo de lesiones por desequilibrio.
nursing_care: Evaluar audición y equilibrio cada turno.
Monitorear niveles séricos de fármacos y función renal.
Observar signos de ototoxicidad: tinnitus, vértigo, náuseas.
Mantener ambiente seguro: suelos secos, barandillas.
Documentar cambios y notificar al médico.
patient_teaching: Informar sobre síntomas de ototoxicidad y la necesidad de reportarlos.
Enseñar a evitar ruidos fuertes y usar protección auditiva.
Explicar la importancia de los controles de laboratorio.
Indicar no interrumpir medicación sin autorización médica.
Recomendar técnicas de seguridad al levantarse y caminar.

outcomes: Integridad física: sin lesiones durante la hospitalización
Seguridad: sin caídas reportadas en 48 horas

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de audición y equilibrio cada turno
interventions.rationale: Detectar cambios tempranos que puedan provocar caídas

interventions.action: Mantener el área del paciente libre de obstáculos y usar barandillas
interventions.rationale: Reducir el riesgo de tropiezos y caídas

interventions.action: Monitorear niveles séricos de vancomicina/aminoglucósidos y función renal
interventions.rationale: Prevenir acumulación del fármaco y daño adicional

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre reportar tinnitus o vértigo inmediatamente
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana para evitar lesiones

interventions.action: Colaborar con el médico para ajustar dosis o cambiar el fármaco si aparecen signos de ototoxicidad
interventions.rationale: Detener la causa del daño reduce la progresión

outcomes: Capacidad de realizar actividades de la vida diaria: 80% del nivel basal en 72 horas
Nivel de energía: sin aumento de fatiga reportada

interventions.action: Planificar actividades en períodos de menor vértigo (ej. sentarse antes de levantarse)
interventions.rationale: Minimiza la intensidad de los síntomas y mejora la tolerancia

interventions.action: Proveer descansos frecuentes y posición semisentada
interventions.rationale: Reduce la fatiga y previene mareos

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración profunda para controlar náuseas
interventions.rationale: Alivia síntomas vestibulares y mejora la participación

interventions.rationale: La deshidratación agrava el vértigo y la intolerancia

interventions.rationale: Fortalece el sistema vestibular y aumenta la tolerancia a la actividad

en.summary: Damage to the sensory cells of the inner ear caused by certain drugs or chemicals, resulting in hearing loss and balance disturbances.
key_points: Aminoglycosides and vancomycin are the most common drugs.
Damage to cochlear hair cells is usually irreversible.
Symptoms include tinnitus, hearing loss, and vertigo.
Monitoring serum levels and renal function reduces risk.
Prevention includes avoiding loud noises and adjusting doses.

pathophysiology: Accumulation of the drug in the endolymphatic fluid damages the cochlear and vestibular hair cells.
Oxidative stress and apoptosis of sensory cells occur.
Vestibular toxicity produces vertigo and imbalance.
risk_factors: Exposure to solvents (toluene) or heavy metals.
signs_symptoms: Progressive hearing loss, initially at high frequencies.
Vertigo or feeling that everything is spinning.
Nausea, vomiting, and imbalance when walking.
Feeling of fullness in the ear.
diagnostics: Serum levels of vancomycin or aminoglycosides.
Otoscopic exam to rule out other causes.
Renal panel (creatinine, BUN) to adjust dose.
treatment: Discontinue or reduce the dose of the ototoxic agent.
Adequate hydration and correction of renal function.
Audiologic therapy (hearing aids) if loss is permanent.
Avoid exposure to loud noises and additional ototoxins.
complications: Chronic vestibular damage with fall risk.
Increased risk of injury from imbalance.
nursing_care: Assess hearing and balance each shift.
Monitor serum drug levels and renal function.
Observe for signs of ototoxicity: tinnitus, vertigo, nausea.
Maintain a safe environment: dry floors, handrails.
Document changes and notify the physician.
patient_teaching: Inform about ototoxicity symptoms and the need to report them.
Teach avoidance of loud noises and use of hearing protection.
Explain the importance of laboratory monitoring.
Advise not to discontinue medication without medical authorization.
Recommend safety techniques when standing and walking.

outcomes: Physical integrity: no injuries during hospitalization
Safety: no falls reported in 48 hours

interventions.action: Assess hearing and balance each shift
interventions.rationale: Detect early changes that may lead to falls

interventions.action: Keep the patient area free of obstacles and use handrails
interventions.rationale: Reduce risk of tripping and falling

interventions.action: Monitor serum levels of vancomycin/aminoglycosides and renal function
interventions.rationale: Prevent drug accumulation and additional damage

interventions.action: Educate the patient to report tinnitus or vertigo immediately
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention to prevent injuries

interventions.action: Collaborate with the physician to adjust dose or change medication if ototoxicity signs appear
interventions.rationale: Stopping the cause of damage reduces progression

outcomes: Ability to perform activities of daily living: 80% of baseline level in 72 hours
Energy level: no reported increase in fatigue

interventions.action: Plan activities during periods of less vertigo (e.g., sit before standing)
interventions.rationale: Minimizes symptom intensity and improves tolerance

interventions.action: Provide frequent rest breaks and semi‑seated position
interventions.rationale: Reduces fatigue and prevents dizziness

interventions.action: Teach deep breathing techniques to control nausea
interventions.rationale: Alleviates vestibular symptoms and improves participation

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and hydration level
interventions.rationale: Dehydration worsens vertigo and intolerance

interventions.action: Coordinate with physiotherapy for safe balance exercises
interventions.rationale: Strengthens vestibular system and increases activity tolerance

summary.0.quote: However, the common pathway involves damage to the sensory cells (hair cells) of the cochlea or vestibular system in the inner ear.

key_points.2.quote: This damage disrupts the normal transmission of sound signals or balance information to the brain, resulting in hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, or imbalance.

key_points.3.quote: They are entirely renally eliminated, and renal function must be monitored along with serial serum drug levels to ensure that aminoglycosides do not accumulate in the body.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: This damage disrupts the normal transmission of sound signals or balance information to the brain, resulting in hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, or imbalance.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: The aminoglycosides , including gentamicin, tobramycin, and amikacin, are used commonly in the hospital setting for their broad-spectrum gram-negative activity, including against infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Elevated vancomycin levels are associated with risk for renal injury and hearing damage (ototoxicity).

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Instruct the client to maintain adequate hydration; monitor kidney function for renally eliminated medications, such as penicillins, most cephalosporins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and particularly fluoroquinolones.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Exposure to certain chemicals, such as solvents (e.g., toluene) or heavy metals (e.g., lead or mercury), can also cause ototoxicity.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Tinnitus is a common condition of the inner ear characterized by the perception of ringing, buzzing, hissing, or other sounds in the absence of external auditory stimuli.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Vertigo is the feeling that you or the room is spinning even when nothing is moving.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: You may also have nausea, vomiting , sweating , trouble walking, or ringing in your ears .

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: This can lead to hearing loss , an uncomfortable sensation of fullness in the ear, ear pain, tinnitus (ringing in the ear), and in rare cases dizziness or imbalance.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: Videonystagmography (VNG) (National Library of Medicine) Also in Spanish

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: Ensure that any ordered samples for serum levels of agents such as vancomycin and aminoglycosides are obtained at the intended time so that accurate dosage adjustments can be made.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: To rule out other conditions, such as middle ear infections or foreign bodies, an otoscopy may be necessary.

sections.diagnostics.4.quote: Most cephalosporins, except for ceftriaxone, must be renally dose adjusted to avoid adverse effects in clients with renal insufficiency.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Instruct the client to maintain adequate hydration; monitor kidney function for renally eliminated medications, such as penicillins, most cephalosporins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and particularly fluoroquinolones.

sections.treatment.2.quote: In cases where the tympanic membrane perforation results in significant hearing loss, the use of hearing aids or other assistive devices may be recommended.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: The aminoglycosides work by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. They are entirely renally eliminated, and renal function must be monitored along with serial serum drug levels to ensure that aminoglycosides do not accumulate in the body.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: If any concerning signs arise, notify the health-care provider promptly.

sections.nursing_care.5.quote: This involved collaborating with the hospital's audiology department.
